org.name: Cinder Peaks Community Foundation
org.tagline: Growing generosity across Arizona's high country
org.mission: Cinder Peaks Community Foundation connects people who care with causes that matter, building lasting resources so that every community in northern Arizona can thrive for generations.
org.vision: A high country where every family has a stable home, a healthy start, meaningful work, and a voice in the decisions that shape their community.

values.name: Rooted in place
values.text: We listen first to the people who live and work in the communities we serve, from the Grand Canyon's rim to the White Mountains.

values.name: Equity in practice
values.text: We direct resources toward communities that have historically been left out of philanthropy, including tribal nations and rural towns.

values.name: Long-term stewardship
values.text: We manage charitable funds prudently so that today's generosity keeps working decades from now.

values.name: Trust and transparency
values.text: We publish our grantmaking, financial information, and decision processes so applicants and donors know how we work.

news.title: Fall 2026 Community Impact awards reach 46 organizations
news.summary: The Foundation's board approved $612,500 in general operating support for arts, education, environment, and animal welfare organizations across all four counties.
body: Forty-six organizations received Fall 2026 Community Impact Grants, ranging from a volunteer-run library in Fredonia to a youth orchestra in Prescott Valley. One third of this year's grantees are first-time recipients.

The Spring 2027 cycle, which funds health, human services, and economic opportunity, opens on February 1, 2027. Applicants can review the guidelines now on the Community Impact Grants: Spring Cycle page.

news.title: New brief maps the infant care gap in northern Arizona
news.summary: Research commissioned by the First Steps Infant & Toddler Fund finds just one licensed infant care slot for every five infants in the four-county region.
body: The Northern Arizona Infant Care Gap brief combines state licensing data with interviews from 64 parents and providers. It finds that rural Apache and Navajo counties face the steepest shortages.
The findings will shape First Steps Fund priorities for 2027. The full brief is available in the Resources and Reports library.

news.title: Rapid Response Fund supports monsoon flood recovery
news.summary: Eleven grants totaling $86,000 helped families in Coconino and Navajo counties recover from post-wildfire flooding.
body: Following heavy monsoon rains over recent burn scars, the High Country Rapid Response & Resilience Fund awarded grants to food banks, chapter houses, and volunteer cleanup crews within ten business days of each request.
The fund remains open on a rolling basis for nonprofits and tribal programs responding to declared emergencies.
